subject: Telemetry egress & tracing agreement - handoff and minimal contract
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acmehealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: sec@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry for Redwood private deployment (questions)

Hi Ben (and team),

Thanks for the quick intro last week. To prep for the handoff we need a concise plan for telemetry from our private VPC cluster into our Splunk HEC instance. High level constraints:
- No broad outbound egress (security policy) — any outbound must be to allow-listed IPs/ports.
- Data must be TLS encrypted in transit, mutual auth preferred.
- Logs: app, infra, and inference-audit logs (PII redaction required).
- Traces: 1 in 10 sampling acceptable for prod, 1 in 1 for pre-prod.
- Retention and proof of rotation/audit: we need certificate/key rotation cadence and audit logs for any agent that touches telemetry.

Can you send: an architecture sketch (forwarder vs push), a minimal egress allowlist (IPs/ports and protocols), and a short set of evidence artifacts you can provide for SOC review? Also please confirm whether Redwood's private-forwarder runs as an outbound-initiated connection from our VPC (preferred) or if you can support an inbound tunnel model.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Gomez
Senior Cloud Architect | Acme Health
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry for Redwood private deployment (questions)

Alex — appreciate the clear constraints. Short answers up front:
- Our private-forwarder model initiates outbound TLS (client) from inside the customer VPC to either a Redwood egress endpoint or directly to your Splunk HEC endpoint (customer preference). Outbound-only is supported; we do not require inbound ports to be opened into your VPC.
- Transport: TLS 1.2+ with optional mutual TLS (mTLS). We can provide certs or accept customer-provisioned certs.
- Protocols/ports: preferred is HTTPS to HEC (TCP 443) or syslog over TLS (TCP 6514) — we will provide an allowlist for the egress IPs.
- Evidence: we can provide runbook excerpts, a config example, HEC mapping CSV, and an egress contract draft.

I attached a short checklist that maps your asks to deliverables (telemetry_requirements_checklist.xlsx). Next steps: schedule a technical handoff call with Marissa (solutions) and Mina (security) — are you free Wed or Thu this week?

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
attachments: telemetry_requirements_checklist.xlsx
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acmehealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry for Redwood private deployment (questions)

Alex — quick technical note before we talk:
- Forwarder vs direct HEC: two supported patterns
  * Forwarder-in-VPC (recommended): a lightweight agent (k8s DaemonSet or sidecar) collects logs/traces, performs field redaction and tagging, and sends outbound to your Splunk HEC or to a Redwood egress endpoint. This keeps IP allowlist small and connection outbound-only.
  * Direct HEC push: Redwood runtime pushes events to a customer HEC using a configured HEC token and TLS. Simpler but requires stable endpoint and token management.
- Redaction/mapping: we'll apply a redaction regex step for PII fields and add a redwood.trace_id / redwood.span_id for trace stitching. We recommend a small mapping CSV to align fields (attached splunk_hec_mapping.csv).
- Tracing hooks: we support OTLP over HTTPS and can emit spans with service.name and a sampling-tag. Sample config attached: redwood_private_forwarder_config_example.yaml — includes HEC URL, TLS settings, and sampling policy.

I'll add a short runbook link here for pre-prod steps: https://drive.redwood/teams/solutions/acme-telemetry-handoff (read-only link). I can walk through this on the call.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_private_forwarder_config_example.yaml, splunk_hec_mapping.csv
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: sec@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry for Redwood private deployment (questions)

Thanks Marissa — that all sounds sensible. A couple clarifications before the call:
1) Egress allowlist: can you publish a fixed set of IPs we can allow, or is it DNS-based and potentially changing? We need stable CIDR/IPs for firewall policies.
2) mTLS: if we manage certs, do you support cert pinning on your endpoint?
3) Evidence for SOC: for pre-prod we'd like a minimal handoff plan (1 page) that covers expected artifact delivery (config files, HEC mapping, rotation schedule) and a short test plan that validates log integrity and trace stitching.

If you can provide the allowlist and the 1-page handoff by EOD Friday, we can greenlight the pre-prod work that starts next week.

Alex
From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acmehealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry egress & tracing agreement - draft egress contract

Alex/Ben — looping in a draft egress/telemetry contract for SOC review. High level items included:
- Egress model: outbound-only client initiated TLS from customer VPC to allow-listed endpoints
- Approved transports: HTTPS/OTLP over 443, syslog-tls on 6514 (mutual TLS optional)
- Evidence bundle: cert chain, HEC token rotation notes, agent audit logs for config changes (90-day window), sample syslog payloads, mapping CSV
- Data controls: configurable PII redaction rules, field-level allowlist/denylist, and sampling policy for traces
- Key rotation: recommend 90-day rotation cycle for HEC tokens and certs where applicable; provide rotation proof logs on request
- Incident escalation: contact list + SLA for forensic evidence (48 hrs for initial artifacts)

Attached: egress_contract_draft.pdf. This is intentionally concise — if Acme has legal/security standard language you want included we can slot it in.

Mina Haddad
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

If that matches your expectations, reply-all with a quick confirmation and we will file the HubSpot task (HS-ACME-2483) and create a short runbook for the pre-prod validation steps.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
